newsitem.title: USA: CBOT-CME seen moving closer to common banking.
newsitem.headline: CBOT-CME seen moving closer to common banking.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) and Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) are expected to move closer toward establishing a common banking system when their joint strategic initiatives committee meets Thursday afternoon, sources close to the committee said.
Several industry sources said CBOT, CME and CBOT's clearinghouse, Board of Trade Clearing Corp (BOTCC), will sign a letter of intent at Thursday's committee meeting to pursue common banking.
"We intend to sign a letter of intent with regards to common banking," said one exchange member who serves on the committee's group on clearing issues.

In late July, the three entities said they would soon sign a letter of intent to pursue common banking initiatives. The CBOT and CME formed the joint strategic committee in January 1996 to explore the possibility of merging operations.
"Once the letter is signed, proposals will be put in place to make common banking possible," a CBOT staff member said.
Common banking would allow a member of the CBOT and CME to use one account when transacting business at either exchange.
One banking account would primarily lower transactions costs for futures commission merchants (FCMs), as most FCMs are dual members.

Les Rosenthal, general partner of Rosenthal-Collins Group and member of the joint strategic committee, said Electronic Data Systems (EDS), an outside consultant, would update the full committee on Thursday on potential savings from a common data processing and clearing system. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
